## speaking-frequency

Term: Speaking frequency
Aliases: turn share
Definition: The number of speaking turns a participant takes in a meeting, counted without weighting longer turns.
Origin: src: sources/interview-guide.md#turns
Distinctions: Unlike [felt safety](#felt-safety), this is a count an observer can record rather than a participant's report.
[proposed]

## dissent

Term: Dissent
Aliases: expressed disagreement
Definition: An utterance that names a disagreement with a decision the group had already taken.
Origin: own-definition
Distinctions: A high [speaking frequency](#speaking-frequency) does not establish dissent, and a proposal can be taken up without anyone disagreeing.
[proposed]

## proposal-uptake

Term: Proposal uptake
Aliases: uptake
Definition: The extent to which a proposal made in one meeting becomes a topic of work in a later one.
Origin: own-definition
Distinctions: Unlike [dissent](#dissent), uptake is about what the group did with a proposal rather than about who disagreed.
[proposed]

## felt-safety

Term: Felt safety
Aliases: perceived safety
Definition: A participant's reported expectation that raising a concern will not expose them to interpersonal harm.
Origin: src: sources/interview-guide.md#safety
Distinctions: Unlike [speaking frequency](#speaking-frequency), this is a report rather than a count, and the two can move in opposite directions.
[proposed]
